PullRequest.Title: Escape hides the classic empty editor hint for this document
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #349451

A new untitled file shows a one-line hint ("Generate code (Ctrl+I), or select a language (Ctrl+K M). Start typing to dismiss or don't show this again."). Until now it could only be dismissed by typing, or turned off everywhere. With this change, Escape in the editor hides it for that document only, like the experimental list-of-actions hint (`workbench.editor.experimental.emptyEditorHintActions`, https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/347850) already does.

- Not persisted: the document is remembered in the same per-model set the list UI uses, so a new untitled file shows the hint again.
- Same keybinding as before (`editor.action.hideEmptyEditorHint`), below other editor contributions, so suggest, find, etc. close first; not active with a selection or multiple cursors.
- The context key `emptyEditorHintActionsVisible` becomes `emptyEditorHintVisible`, set by the contribution while either variant is shown. Both variants close through one method (`closeHint`).
- Telemetry: the classic hint logs the `emptyEditorHint` action `closeEscape` with variant `classic`; the classification comment is updated.

The list UI is unchanged (Escape in the editor or in the hint still hides it and logs `closeEscape` with variant `actions`).

## Demo

Code OSS built from this branch: Escape hides the classic hint, typing and deleting in the same file does not bring it back, a new untitled file shows it again, and the list of actions still closes on Escape.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9887e489-1ce6-4636-8640-c5b2053d3093

## Validation

- New unit test for the classic hint (`emptyEditorHintActions.test.ts`): visible initially, hidden after Escape, stays hidden after editing the same document, shown for another document, and the `shown`/`closeEscape` telemetry with variant `classic`. The existing list-of-actions test passes.
- `tsgo` workbench typecheck (`src/tsconfig.json`) and oxlint on the changed files.
- Code OSS from this branch (recording above). The telemetry log contains `emptyEditorHint` with `action: closeEscape` for both `variant: classic` and `variant: actions`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an empty editor and display the classic or classic-Markdown hint; process subsequent model, decoration, and configuration changes.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing eagerly instantiated contribution evaluates eligibility and creates one content widget when needed. The diff adds one editor-scoped context key and sets it when creating the widget; it adds no awaited initialization. Telemetry delivery is off the rendering critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Sanitize and enrich the fixed-field hint telemetry payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing shown event per widget creation; no added shown events or document-content serialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Widget construction already emitted the same shown event with the same payload fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Local payload preparation is synchronous; downstream delivery is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deliver enabled desktop telemetry to the shared-process telemetry channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One channel call per delivered existing shown event, subject to telemetry-level, metered-connection, and startup-buffer gating.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same hint-created telemetry already used this channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The channel promise is not awaited by widget construction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit enabled telemetry to the existing SDK transport or remote telemetry provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One event submission per existing shown event, not a newly forced HTTP request; SDK initialization is shared through _asyncAiCore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same shown telemetry used the same transport before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Transport completion and SDK initialization are not awaited by rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of live code editors and eligibility-change events; existing agent and editor-registration scans are unchanged. The added state is one boolean context key per editor and one small close callback per classic widget.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Eligibility checks and widget creation execute synchronously on the UI thread. A contribution retains at most one hint widget. Existing update events do not reconstruct a widget when its variant remains unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The current widget is reused across same-variant updates. Visibility writes notify only on actual value changes, as Context.setValue compares the old and new boolean. The closed-model WeakSet already existed; new classic dismissal also uses it. No new heavyweight cache or negatively cached remote request is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced eager registration, eligibility guards, widget reuse, value-change suppression, disposal, and telemetry dispatch. Existing editor-resolution and widget rendering paths retain their previous frequency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timing measurements; context-notification cost depends on editor-local listeners. No changed scaling mechanism for heavyweight work was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: bounded context state and callback allocation enable the feature without adding expensive initialization or repeated rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Press Escape to dismiss a classic hint, continue typing and clearing that document, then open another document.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The keybinding resolves the focused editor's contribution; closeHint logs one action, records the current model weakly, disposes the widget, and resets visibility. Only fixed-size telemetry preparation and local disposal precede completion; telemetry delivery is not awaited.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create, sanitize, and enrich a fixed-field closeEscape telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional action event for each explicit classic/classicMarkdownEditor dismissal; zero further events from repeated Escape after dismissal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Escape did not dismiss the classic hint or emit this classic closeEscape action event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous payload preparation happens before local widget disposal; no model contents are serialized.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the enabled classic closeEscape event through the existing desktop telemetry channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one extra telemetry channel call per explicit classic dismissal after existing telemetry gating; no per-model collection fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no classic closeEscape event; actions-variant dismissal already emitted one.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delivery is fire-and-forget and does not block dismissal on the response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit the classic closeEscape event to existing enabled telemetry transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional event submission per explicit classic dismissal; no flush or independent SDK initialization is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Classic Escape supplied no telemetry event to the transport; the actions variant already did.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Network delivery is off the dismissal critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct explicitly dismissed models per editor contribution, rather than every keypress or all open documents. The added action telemetry occurs once per actual classic dismissal.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One focused-editor handler runs synchronously. The reset context key disables subsequent Escape invocation for that hint, and closedForModels prevents recreating it for the same model within that contribution.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing WeakSet now suppresses classic hints too. It retains no strong model references, is not persisted, and new model identity remains eligible. getUntitledDocumentId performs an existing ResourceMap lookup, with missing IDs returning undefined rather than triggering discovery or I/O.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced command conditions, closeHint, classic close, hideForModel, WeakSet eligibility, widget removal and listener disposal, ResourceMap ID lookup, and non-awaited telemetry appenders.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact telemetry overhead is unmeasured and deployment-dependent, but event cardinality is bounded by explicit dismissals rather than input frequency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: intentional fixed-size telemetry is bounded to actual dismissals, and weak ownership plus disposal prevents model or widget retention.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display, resize, switch, and dismiss the experimental actions hint, including fallback to the classic hint in a small editor.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing actions widget builds a bounded set of rows, measures its height, and either stays mounted or is disposed in favor of the classic widget. The contribution now owns the visibility key. Escape and the close button use the same previous telemetry/focus/disposal flow through a shared callback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read DOM offsetHeight after setting width and position the overlay widget.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing measurement on construction and layout/row-update events; unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same width write, height measurement, fit calculation, and fallback existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous layout remains on the rendering/resize path, but its frequency and input size are not increased.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit existing actions close/closeEscape telemetry through the desktop channel when enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing action event per dismissal, plus existing shown telemetry on successful widget creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The actions widget already logged the action before invoking its close callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delivery is not awaited by dismissal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Deliver the existing actions-hint telemetry through the configured transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Unchanged event submissions for shown and explicit actions; no new flush or transport initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical actions telemetry used the same transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delivery remains off the rendering and dismissal critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible editor count, resize events, and existing agent/editor-registration changes. The list has a bounded number of action rows; no new per-registration or per-document boundary fan-out is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering and layout execute synchronously on the UI thread; one hint widget is retained per contribution. Context-driven row rerendering filters specifically for ChatContextKeys.enabled, so the renamed visibility key does not trigger row reconstruction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing actionsRequiredSize prevents repeatedly constructing an actions widget while the editor remains too small. Existing widget reuse and weak closed-model suppression are preserved. Visibility binding moves from widget creation to contribution creation; no accumulating binding or disposable is created on each reconstruction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced fit fallback, actionsRequiredSize, context-event filtering, close callbacks, and DisposableStore cleanup. Reopener command execution and storage writes remain confined to unchanged explicit action handlers, not the changed visibility/dismissal path.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Existing synchronous layout duration varies with browser state and editor count; the changed code does not increase the measurement count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: visibility ownership is centralized without amplifying layout, command execution, telemetry, or retained resources.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open editor accessibility help and resolve the new Escape instruction's keybinding.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The help provider assembles its existing text and adds one localized sentence in editable editors. The existing resolver performs one additional local keybinding lookup before rendering the help into an in-memory text model.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: User-requested help openings or refreshes, existing fixed-size help text, and one extra keybinding marker. Work does not scale with workspace files, document contents, or number of open editors.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Content assembly and keybinding resolution run synchronously. _getTextModel returns an existing model or creates one locally; its promise is not a filesystem/network read. The existing new-untitled command is awaited only when there is no active/focused code editor.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The accessible-view model uses a stable provider URI and is reused when live; its text is replaced only when different. Keybinding resolution uses the existing service. No additional external cache, model per sentence, or persistent state is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced provideContent, resolveContentAndKeybindingItems, accessible-view rendering, and _getTextModel. These paths perform local model operations; the diff adds no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measurements of help rendering; the change adds one bounded sentence, one lookup, and one configured/unconfigured-keybinding item.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: bounded extra help content does not change rendering frequency, model lifetime, or external-boundary cardinality.
